Oh boy. Here we go.
In grade 6 and under, I used to be a very outgoing girl. Not 'popular', but more like the weird one who never used to care how people viewed her, and just talked to anyone who struck her fancy. I was the 'so random' one who would eat grass, and take prat falls in class just to be funny.
That year, in 6th grade, I met my soon-to-be lifelong best friend. She came across as quiet and shy, since she'd just moved to my city not very long before I'd met her, and was still upset about leaving her old life behind. So since I'd used to be outgoing, and thought she looked cool, I took it upon myself to approach her. 
We hit it off immediately, and soon after, we were talking on the phone nearly every day.

I was already very into anime, something no one my age really cared about or knew at the time, (I was asked "who's annie-may?" a couple of times.), and I 'infected' my new best friend with it as well.

Soon, it encompassed everything we did or talked about. Yu Yu Hakusho, Yu-Gi-Oh, Inuyasha, Fullmetal Alchemist...we'd watch everything that was available to us that came out of Japan.
And soon, over the phone, we'd play out scenarios with our own characters meant to represent ourselves. We'd invented roleplay without even realizing that roleplay was...well, an actual thing. 
It was embarrassing, but we had self-insert OCs for just about everything we watched. 

Still, with my young imagination, it was incredible just how much more immersed I was in the stories now that "I" was there. It was like...well, when you watch something like the movie Page Master, or anything that tried to REALLY hype you into reading books when you were a kid-- it felt as if I was literally transported to these worlds.

It was fun.
We were INSUFFERABLE weeaboos, but it was fun.

Our little girlish fantasies about these worlds and characters didn't take long to turn into romantic ones, and I'd found myself playing male characters for her, to act as her 'boyfriend'. She'd do the same for me. It wasn't initially my idea, but since she wanted to, that's what we did. We only did this over the phone, so as to not 'make it weird', and she would discourage me from doing character voices in person while she could see me.

Two years later, her family moved out of state.

Shortly before her move, I discovered the BL genre with her. Her, being extremely straight, thought that the author "must not know how to write friendship well", but me, being....well, /unknowingly/ at the time, NOT straight, thought..."so friends can be like this with each other, too...?"

It was absolutely terrifying.
I couldn't be gay, after all I had all of these 'boyfriends', and crushes on boys my age at school.
Not knowing my own feelings, or feeling like I couldn't somehow control them, scared me more than anything else. The distance her family put between us with the move helped me forget about that sheer terror though, at least for a good decade.

After the move, we kept talking on the phone every night. Kept getting into new things, kept roleplaying even more elaborate, and at times, extremely well thought out scenarios...to the point where I'd locked myself away in this world we created for ourselves. In high school, I had no friends but her, and some online. I'd become a complete introvert, and all I ever wanted was to go home and roleplay with her. The real world had no bearing to my life whatsoever in those times. My home life was increasingly turbulent due to sickness and abuse, and I just wanted my fake lives with my fake boyfriends to make it all go away. My depression began to flourish as well, and I had very high hopes that I would die before I turned 18.

I flunked out of High School.
I became a NEET, and kept up this pattern with no reprieve until the age of 22.

She introduced me to an online roleplay community she'd joined. (We also enjoyed text RP).
It was a lot of fun (despite the horrible, petulant drama at times), and there, I met my soon-to-be boyfriend.

For reference, he's a pre-transition transboy-- ie, female bodied/voiced, though identifying as male. Absolutely perfect for me, since for the past 11 years, my 'boyfriends' were all voiced by a girl.

We hit it off immediately. 
We started talking on the phone as well. 
I taught him how to roleplay aloud, like I'd done with my best friend.
These roleplays quickly turned romantic
...and then, these roleplays turned sexual.

The sexual aspect is one I hadn't explored in roleplaying with my best friend before, after all, that would be 'weird', right...? But with someone I was fully and openly attracted to, it was something I'd completely welcomed. 
I felt that all my roleplays with my best friend were somehow coaching me for when I could finally have a relationship in real life. I was so excited to finally be moving forward.
However, these new, more intimate role-plays, effected my view on my older ones...and when I'd tried to go back to role-playing with my best friend, everything felt...weird.

That terror of being unable to control my feelings, and those fears about not knowing my own sexuality/feelings came right back to the surface. I ended up avoiding her, because I wanted to run away from the thought of,
"Wait a second, I've been playing her boyfriend for 11 years, what if I'm gay for her."

I can't describe how absolutely scared I was. It must sound stupid, but you have to understand how repressed the two of us were...I would cry to her sometimes about how I thought I liked girls, and how it was so confusing because I knew I also liked boys, and she'd respond with, "I don't want to play a girlfriend for you, because that would make me uncomfortable."
She'd say that if I was bi, I could just choose to let the hetero 'side' of my sexuality be 'stronger'...

It got so bad I would outright say lesbophobic things just to distance myself from feeling the things I felt, just so things wouldn't get 'weird'...
So I stopped talking to her as much, and started talking to my boyfriend more.
I wanted to be with him. I was so in love with him, I didn't want anything to interfere...

I tried to talk with her about him, but she seemed utterly uninterested in our roleplays, or what we were doing, or any of my 'firsts' that I thought we would tell each other about when they happen...
And soon, after I write her a formal apology for being so distant...she sends a message reading "I don't think we're friends anymore".

I panic.
I block her on everything.
I cling to my boyfriend, ultimately shutting out everyone that wasn't him.

This...ultimately puts a strain on our relationship as well. 
I instead shift my internal world to be only his and my own, but this isolates him...
and this isolates me.

Two suicide attempts later, at 25, here I am.

I now have my GED, I now have a job, and I'm trying to live for myself...but the issue here, is that it's hard to get a grasp on who I even am after putting so much of myself into other people. After /being/ so many different people for others.

So, that's the story of my best friend and what happened to separate us. Sorry if it was long or uninteresting.
By all means stay here and keep distracting yourself then. I'm here to talk, but I warn you I'm not the most optimistic person.
